title: 2026 Pulitzer Prizes announced
text:
The Pulitzer Prize Board announced the 2026 Pulitzer Prizes on 4 May 2026. In journalism, the Minnesota Star Tribune staff won Breaking News Reporting, and Mark Lamster of The Dallas Morning News won Criticism. Aaron Parsley of Texas Monthly won Feature Writing. The Washington Post won Public Service, with The Wall Street Journal and the Chicago Tribune as finalists. The New York Times staff won Investigative Reporting, with ProPublica's Debbie Cenziper, Megan Rose and Brandon Roberts as finalists. Reuters staff won National Reporting.

In the arts, Bess Wohl won the Drama prize for Liberation, a play that examines the legacy of the consciousness-raising feminist groups of the 1970s. Daniel Kraus won the Fiction prize for Angel Down, a World War I novel told in a single sentence. The judges called it a stylistic tour-de-force that blends allegory, magical realism and science fiction into a cohesive whole. Jill Lepore won the History prize for We the People: A History of the U.S. Constitution.

Drama and fiction winners each receive a $15,000 award.
writer_flags: Passage is about 185 words; only facts with two publishers are included, so it falls short of the 220-word floor
Judges' quote 'stylistic tour-de-force' rests on mande.net plus the iSchool page; second source is thin
Fiction and Drama $15,000 award: iSchool (fiction) and Playbill (drama) only
Q1 Columbia administers the Pulitzers: idealist and academia-lab only; pulitzer.org not confirmed for this
Q2 Joseph Pulitzer died 1911: idealist, hungaricana and anniversaire-celebrite; one archival source
Q3 lawsuit against Pulitzer board filed 2022: NPR plus cswnewstest.duckdns.org (unclear publisher)
Q4 Sahitya Akademi / Booker / Goncourt country pairings: encyclopedic and aggregator sources
Q6 Prix Goncourt awarded since 1903: fnac and vikidia; founding dates disputed in sources
Q6 Sahitya Akademi inaugurated 1954: cheggindia and visionias; sources differ on institution year
Q7 Sahitya Akademi first given 1955: single aggregator source
Q7 Booker Prize founded 1969 by Booker McConnell: fantasticfiction and one other
Q7 Prix Goncourt first awarded 1913 is the false statement; relies on 1903 date above
Q8 Booker eligibility (English-language novels): sources partly dated; pre-2014 rules differ

questions.q: Which US university administers the Pulitzer Prizes?
questions.explanation: The Pulitzer Prizes are run by Columbia University, which was made the custodian of the prizes through the bequest of Joseph Pulitzer's estate.

questions.q: In which year did the publisher Joseph Pulitzer, whose estate endowed the Pulitzer Prizes, die?
questions.explanation: Joseph Pulitzer died on 29 October 1911, and his bequest led to the Pulitzer Prizes being established; the first prizes were awarded in 1917.

questions.q: In which year did a sitting US president file a lawsuit against the Pulitzer Prize board over its award of Russia-collusion reporting?
questions.explanation: The lawsuit was filed in 2022 over the board's decision to award reporting on alleged collusion between the 2016 Trump campaign and Russia, and it was still active in May 2026.
The Pulitzer Prize is American (I-D), the Booker Prize is British (II-C), the Prix Goncourt is French (III-B) and the Sahitya Akademi Award is Indian (IV-A).

questions.assertion: Daniel Kraus won the 2026 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction for the novel Angel Down.
questions.reason: The Pulitzer Prize for Fiction is open only to authors who are not citizens of the United States.
questions.explanation: The assertion is true, but the reason is false: the Fiction prize is awarded for distinguished fiction by an American author, so it is not restricted to non-citizens.

statements: I. Joseph Pulitzer was born in the United States.
II. The Sahitya Akademi was inaugurated in 1954.
questions.explanation: Statement I is false because Joseph Pulitzer was born in Makó, Hungary. Statement II is true: the Sahitya Akademi was inaugurated on 12 March 1954, so only II is correct.

statements: 1. The Pulitzer Prizes were first awarded in 1917.
2. The Sahitya Akademi Award was first given in 1955.
3. The Booker Prize was founded in 1969 by Booker McConnell, a company.
4. The Prix Goncourt was first awarded in 1913.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct, and statement 4 is wrong because the Prix Goncourt was first awarded in December 1903. Three statements are correct, so the answer is Only three.

statements: I. The Prix Goncourt is awarded by the Academie Goncourt.
II. The Booker Prize is open only to novels written in English.
III. The Booker Prize is open only to novels written in French.
questions.explanation: Statement I is true, as the Academie Goncourt gives the prize. Statement II is true because Booker Prize novels are written in English. Statement III is false, so the correct answer is I and II only.
